chapters.title: The God of All Comfort
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 1

Greeting

1Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Timothy, to the church of God that is in Corinth, with all the saints throughout Achaia:

2grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

The God of All Comfort

3Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and God of all comfort,

4who comforts us in all our trouble, so that we can comfort those who are in any trouble with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

5For as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so through Christ our comfort overflows too.

6If we are troubled, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which works in you when you patiently endure the same sufferings that we suffer.

7Our hope for you is firm, for we know that as you share in our sufferings, so you also share in our comfort.

8We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the trouble we went through in Asia. We were so utterly weighed down, beyond our strength, that we despaired even of life.

9Indeed, we felt within ourselves that we had received the sentence of death, so that we would not rely on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.

10He rescued us from so deadly a peril, and He will rescue us; on Him we have set our hope that He will rescue us again,

11as you also help us by your prayers, so that many will give thanks on our behalf for the gift granted us through the prayers of many.

Yes in Christ

12For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience: that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and above all toward you, with holiness and godly sincerity, not by earthly wisdom but by the grace of God.

13For we write you nothing other than what you read and understand, and I hope you will understand fully,

14as you have understood us in part, that we are your boast as you are ours on the day of our Lord Jesus.

15Sure of this, I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace.

16I meant to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to come back to you from Macedonia and have you send me on my way to Judea.

17When I wanted to do this, did I make my plans lightly? Or do I make my plans by worldly standards, ready to say "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at once?

18As God is faithful, our word to you has not been "Yes" and "No."

19For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we preached among you, Silvanus and Timothy and I, was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it has always been "Yes."

20For all the promises of God find their "Yes" in Him. That is why it is through Him that we say our "Amen" to God, for His glory.

21It is God who makes us firm with you in Christ, and who has anointed us;

22He has also sealed us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge.

23I call on God as witness against my soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.

24Not that we lord it over your faith; we work with you for your joy, for you stand firm in your faith.

Notes

  • vv3–7 "the God of all comfort, who comforts us… so that we can comfort" — paraklēsis and parakaleō, comfort, ten times in five verses. It is Isaiah's word in the Greek, Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1), and I, I am He who comforts you (51:12); and the word of the Advocate, paraklētos, whom Jesus promised (John 14:16). The comfort Paul receives is not for him to keep: it overflows to others as Christ's sufferings overflow to him.

  • vv19–20 "in Him it has always been 'Yes'… through Him that we say our 'Amen'" — Amen is a Hebrew word, from the root of being firm and sure (the trusted of Genesis 15:6). Isaiah calls the LORD Elohei amen, the God of truth, word for word the God of Amen (Isaiah 65:16). Every promise God made is Yes in Christ, and the church answers it with Amen.

  • vv21–22 "makes us firm… in Christ, and who has anointed us… sealed us and given us the Spirit… as a pledge" — Christon… chrisas: Christ means the Anointed, and God has anointed those who are in Him. Arrabōn, pledge, is a Hebrew word in Greek letters, the pledge Judah left with Tamar, Your seal and your cord, and your staff (Genesis 38:18), in the Greek arrabōn. The seal and the pledge there were the token that the full payment would come; here the Spirit is that token.

chapters.title: The Aroma of Christ
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 2

The Letter Written in Tears

1For I made up my mind not to come to you again in sorrow.

2If I cause you sorrow, who is there to make me glad but the one I have made sorrowful?

3I wrote as I did so that when I came I would not be made sorrowful by those who should have made me rejoice, for I am confident about all of you, that my joy is the joy of you all.

4For I wrote to you out of much trouble and anguish of heart and with many tears, not to cause you sorrow but to let you know the love I have, more than enough, for you.

Forgive Him

5If anyone has caused sorrow, he has caused it not to me but in some measure, not to overstate it, to all of you.

6The punishment given by the majority is enough for such a man,

7so that now you should rather forgive and comfort him, or he may be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.

8So I urge you to confirm your love for him.

9For this is why I wrote: to test you and see whether you are obedient in everything.

10Anyone you forgive, I forgive too. What I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven for your sake in the presence of Christ,

11so that we would not be outwitted by Satan, for we are not unaware of his schemes.

Led in Triumph

12When I came to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ, though a door was opened for me in the Lord,

13my spirit had no rest because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.

14But thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in His triumphal procession, and through us spreads everywhere the aroma of the knowledge of Him.

15For we are the fragrance of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing,

16to the one an aroma from death to death, to the other an aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?

17For we are not like so many, peddling the word of God, but as men of sincerity, as from God, we speak before God in Christ.

Notes

  • v14 "who in Christ always leads us in His triumphal procession" — thriambeuonti, the word of a victor's march through the city with his captives behind him; Paul uses it once more, of God leading the rulers and authorities in triumph over them (Colossians 2:15). Whether Paul sees himself as a captive led in Christ's train or as a soldier sharing the victory, the verb does not say; either way the triumph is God's.

  • vv14–16 "the aroma of the knowledge of Him… the fragrance of Christ to God… an aroma from death to death… from life to life" — osmē, aroma, and euōdia, fragrance, are the two words of the Law's soothing aroma to the LORD, osmē euōdias in the Greek (Leviticus 1:9), the smoke of the offering rising to God. Paul splits the phrase between his three lines: the apostles themselves are the offering, and the same smell is life to some and death to others.

chapters.title: The Veil Removed
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 3

A Letter from Christ

1Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

2You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

3You show that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of hearts of flesh.

4Such is the confidence we have through Christ toward God.

5Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to reckon anything as coming from us; our sufficiency is from God,

6who has made us sufficient to be ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

The Greater Glory

7Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the sons of Israel could not look steadily at Moses' face because of its glory, a glory that was being done away with,

8will not the ministry of the Spirit have even more glory?

9For if there was glory in the ministry that brought condemnation, the ministry that brings righteousness overflows with far more glory.

10Indeed, what once had glory has no glory at all in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it.

11For if what was being done away with came with glory, much more will what remains have glory.

The Veil

12Since we have such a hope, we are very bold,

13not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not look steadily at the end of what was being done away with.

14But their minds were hardened. For to this very day, when the old covenant is read, that same veil remains, not lifted, because only in Christ is it done away with.

15Yes, to this day whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts.

16But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

17Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

18We all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another, as from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

Notes

  • v3 "not on tablets of stone but on tablets of hearts of flesh" — the two covenants side by side. The first was tablets of stone, written by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18); the new is the promise of Ezekiel, I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh (Ezekiel 36:26), and of Jeremiah, on their heart I will write it (Jeremiah 31:33).

  • vv7, 13 "the glory of his face… a veil over his face" — Exodus 34:29–35 in the Greek, where the skin of his face was glorified, dedoxastai. The Hebrew says the skin of his face had grown horns, qaran (see the note there), and the Greek is the reading Paul builds on. Exodus says Moses veiled his face after speaking to the people; it does not say the glory faded. That is Paul's reading, set against the glory that remains (v11).

  • vv14–17 "when the old covenant is read… whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit" — tēs palaias diathēkēs, the old covenant, a phrase found only here in the New Testament. V16 is Exodus 34:34 in the Greek, When Moses went in before the LORD… he would take the veil off, with Moses went in changed to anyone turns. The Lord of that verse is YHWH, and Paul says who He is now met as: the Lord is the Spirit.

  • v18 "beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror" — katoptrizomenoi, in the New Testament only here, from katoptron, mirror. It can mean beholding as in a mirror, as Paul's we see in a mirror (1 Corinthians 13:12), or reflecting, as Moses' face shone back what it had seen. Metamorphoumetha, are being transformed, is the verb of Jesus transfigured (Mark 9:2) and of Romans 12:2.

chapters.title: Treasure in Clay Pots
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 4

Light Out of Darkness

1Therefore, since we have this ministry by the mercy of God, we do not lose heart.

2We have renounced the shameful things that are done in secret. We do not use cunning or distort the word of God, but by openly stating the truth we commend ourselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God.

3Even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

4In their case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that they do not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

5For what we proclaim is not ourselves but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake.

6For God, who said, "Light will shine out of darkness," is the one who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

Treasure in Clay Pots

7But we have this treasure in clay pots, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us.

8We are troubled on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

9persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed;

10always carrying in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be shown in our bodies.

11For we who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be shown in our mortal flesh.

12So death is at work in us, but life in you.

13Since we have the same Spirit of faith that is in what is written, "I believed, therefore I spoke," we also believe, and therefore we speak,

14knowing that He who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus and bring us with you into His presence.

15All this is for your sake, so that as grace reaches more and more people, it may increase thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

The Eternal Weight of Glory

16So we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day.

17For this light and momentary trouble is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison,

18as we look not to what is seen but to what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

Notes

  • vv4, 6 "Christ, who is the image of God… God, who said, 'Light will shine out of darkness'… in the face of Jesus Christ" — the first day of creation, "Light — be." And light was (Genesis 1:3), joined to Isaiah's The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light (Isaiah 9:2), whose Greek has the same verb, light will shine on you. The God who made light at the beginning has made it shine again in the heart. The image of God is the word of humankind's making (Genesis 1:27), and the face is the answer to the veiled face of Moses (3:13): the glory once hidden is seen in Christ's face.

  • v13 "I believed, therefore I spoke" — Psalm 116:10 in the Greek. The Hebrew reads I believed, even when I said, "I am greatly afflicted": the psalmist kept faith in his suffering. Paul, troubled on every side (v8), takes up the same words.

  • v17 "an eternal weight of glory" — in Hebrew, kavod, glory, is from kaved, heavy, the word of Moses' heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue (Exodus 4:10). Paul sets the light, elaphron, trouble of now against glory that has weight.

chapters.title: A New Creation
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 5

The Earthly Tent

1For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is taken down, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

2In this tent we groan, longing to put on our dwelling from heaven,

3if indeed, once we have put it on, we will not be found naked.

4For while we are still in this tent, we groan, weighed down, because we do not want to be unclothed but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

5It is God who has prepared us for this very thing, and who has given us the Spirit as a pledge.

6So we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord,

7for we walk by faith, not by sight.

8We are confident, I say, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

9So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to please Him.

10For all of us must appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for what he has done in the body, whether good or bad.

The Love of Christ Compels Us

11Knowing, then, the fear of the Lord, we persuade others. What we are is plain to God, and I hope it is plain to your consciences too.

12We are not commending ourselves to you again, but giving you a reason to boast about us, so that you can answer those who boast in appearances and not in the heart.

13For if we are out of our minds, it is for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for you.

14For the love of Christ compels us, because we are convinced of this: one has died for all; therefore all have died.

15He died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves but for Him who for their sake died and was raised.

A New Creation

16So from now on we regard no one by human standards. Even though we once regarded Christ by human standards, we do not regard Him that way any longer.

17So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: the old things have passed away; new things have come.

18All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:

19that in Christ God was reconciling the world to Himself, not reckoning their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.

20So we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.

21He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "the earthly tent… In this tent we groan, weighed down" — the words of the Wisdom of Solomon, a perishable body weighs down the soul, and this earthly tent burdens the mind (Wisdom 9:15): skēnos, tent, is Wisdom's word, and Paul's baroumenoi, weighed down, is close kin to Wisdom's barynei. Wisdom left the soul burdened; Paul longs not to be unclothed but clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life, the word of 1 Corinthians 15:54.

  • v7 "we walk by faith, not by sight" — ou dia eidous, not by form, the word God used of Moses: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly, en eidei in the Greek, and not in riddles (Numbers 12:8). What Moses had, seeing God's form, believers do not yet have; they walk by faith until they see face to face (1 Corinthians 13:12).

  • v17 "there is a new creation: the old things have passed away; new things have come" — kainē ktisis has no verb: there is a new creation, the world made new, or he is a new creation, the believer made new. Paul's other use is the world's: neither circumcision counts for anything nor uncircumcision, but a new creation (Galatians 6:15). The words are Isaiah's in the Greek, Do not remember… the things of old (ta archaia)… I am about to do a new thing (kaina) (Isaiah 43:18–19).

  • v21 "He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us" — hamartian, sin. In Hebrew one word, chatat, is both sin and sin offering: the anointed priest brings for the sin he has committed… a young bull… as a sin offering, chatato… le-chatat, the same word twice (Leviticus 4:3). So to be sin can mean to bear sin itself, or to be a sin offering, as Romans 8:3 has as an offering for sin. Christ takes the place of sin, and those in Him receive the place of the righteousness of God.

chapters.title: Now Is the Day of Salvation
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 6

Servants of God

1Working together with Him, then, we urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain.

2For He says:
"In a favorable time I listened to you,
and in a day of salvation I helped you."
Now is the favorable time; now is the day of salvation.

3We put no obstacle in anyone's way, so that no fault may be found with our ministry,

4but in every way we commend ourselves as servants of God: by great endurance, in troubles, hardships and distresses,

5in beatings, imprisonments and riots, in labors, sleepless nights and hunger;

6by purity, knowledge, patience and kindness, by the Holy Spirit, by genuine love,

7by the word of truth and the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left;

8through glory and dishonor, through slander and praise; treated as deceivers, and yet true;

9as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and yet we live; as disciplined, and yet not put to death;

10as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.

Open Your Hearts

11We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our heart is wide open.

12You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own affections.

13In return — I speak as to children — open wide your hearts too.

Do Not Be Unequally Yoked

14Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? What fellowship has light with darkness?

15What agreement has Christ with Belial? What share has a believer with an unbeliever?

16What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said:
"I will dwell among them and walk among them,
and I will be their God,
and they will be My people.

17Therefore go out from their midst,
and be separate, says the Lord,
and touch nothing unclean;
then I will welcome you,

18and I will be a father to you,
and you will be My sons and daughters,
says the Lord Almighty."

Notes

  • v2 "In a favorable time I listened to you, and in a day of salvation I helped you" — Isaiah 49:8 in the Greek, where the Hebrew has a day of deliverance, from the servant song in which the LORD gives His servant as a covenant for the people. Paul's answer, now is the day of salvation, puts the Corinthians inside the promise.

  • v9 "as dying, and yet we live; as disciplined, and yet not put to death" — the words of Psalm 118: I will not die, but live… Yah has disciplined me severely, but He has not given me over to death (Psalm 118:17–18), paideuōn epaideusen me in the Greek, the verb Paul has.

  • v14 "Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers" — heterozygountes, yoked with another kind, from the Greek of the Law: You shall not mate your livestock with a different kind, heterozygō (Leviticus 19:19), and You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together (Deuteronomy 22:10). Two animals of different kinds cannot pull one plow.

  • vv15–18 "Belial… I will dwell among them… go out from their midst… I will be a father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters" — Beliar, the Hebrew beliyya'al, worthlessness, the word of the worthless men who were Eli's sons (1 Samuel 2:12), here a name for the enemy of Christ. The promises are strung from the Law and the Prophets: I will walk among you, and I will be your God, and you will be My people (Leviticus 26:12); go out from the middle of her… touch nothing unclean (Isaiah 52:11); and Nathan's word about David's son, I will be his father, and he shall be My son (2 Samuel 7:14), which Paul widens to sons and daughters.

chapters.title: Godly Sorrow
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 7

1Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.

Paul's Joy

2Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have ruined no one, we have taken advantage of no one.

3I do not say this to condemn you, for I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.

4I speak to you with great boldness; I have great pride in you; I am filled with comfort; in all our trouble I am overflowing with joy.

5For even when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest; we were troubled at every turn, fighting without and fears within.

6But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the coming of Titus,

7and not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted by you, as he told us of your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.

Sorrow That Leads to Repentance

8For even if I made you sorrowful with my letter, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it, for I see that the letter made you sorrowful, though only for a while,

9now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt sorrow as God willed, so that you suffered no loss through us.

10For sorrow as God wills produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret, but the sorrow of the world produces death.

11See what earnestness this very thing, sorrow as God wills, has produced in you: what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what readiness to see justice done! In every way you have shown yourselves innocent in the matter.

12So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who was wronged, but so that your earnestness for us might be made plain to you in the sight of God.

13For this reason we are comforted. Besides our own comfort, we rejoiced still more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.

14For if I have boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame; but just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting before Titus has proved true as well.

15His affection for you is all the greater as he remembers the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling.

16I rejoice that I have complete confidence in you.

Notes

  • v6 "God, who comforts the downcast" — Isaiah 49:13 in the Greek, the LORD… has comforted the downcast of His people, tous tapeinous… parekalesen, where the Hebrew has will have compassion on His afflicted. The comfort of chapter 1 comes back in a person: the coming of Titus.

  • vv8–10 "I do not regret it… a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret" — two words. Metamelomai, regret, is the word of Judas, who changed his mind and brought back the silver (Matthew 27:3): sorrow over what has happened. Metanoia, repentance, is a change of mind and direction: sorrow that turns. Paul regretted the letter for a while; the repentance it produced is ametamelētos, a thing no one will ever regret.

chapters.title: The Grace of Giving
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 8

The Example of Macedonia

1We want you to know, brothers, about the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia.

2In a severe test of trouble, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity.

3For they gave as they were able, I can testify, and beyond what they were able, of their own accord,

4begging us earnestly for the grace of sharing in this service to the saints.

5They did not do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, by the will of God.

6So we urged Titus that, as he had begun, so he should also complete among you this act of grace.

7But just as you overflow in everything, in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love we have kindled in you, see that you overflow in this act of grace also.

The Grace of Our Lord

8I do not say this as a command, but to prove by the earnestness of others that your love also is genuine.

9For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, for your sake He became poor, so that by His poverty you might become rich.

10In this matter I give my judgment: it is to your advantage, since last year you were the first not only to act but also to want to act.

11So now finish doing it, so that your readiness in wanting it may be matched by your completing it, out of what you have.

12For if the readiness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what a person has, not according to what he does not have.

13I do not mean that others should be eased and you burdened, but that there should be fairness:

14at the present time your abundance should supply their need, so that their abundance may also supply your need, and so there may be fairness.

15As it is written, "The one who gathered much had nothing over, and the one who gathered little had no lack."

Titus and the Brothers

16Thanks be to God, who put the same earnestness for you into the heart of Titus.

17He not only welcomed our appeal, but being very earnest he is going to you of his own accord.

18With him we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.

19Not only that, he has been appointed by the churches to travel with us as we carry out this act of grace, for the glory of the Lord Himself and to show our readiness.

20We are taking care that no one should blame us about this generous gift that we are administering,

21for we aim at what is honorable not only in the Lord's sight but also in the sight of men.

22With them we are sending our brother, whom we have often tested and found earnest in many matters, and who is now much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.

23As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for your benefit; as for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.

24So show them, in the sight of the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting about you.

Notes

  • vv1, 4, 6–7, 9, 19 "the grace of God… the grace of sharing… this act of grace… the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ" — charis, grace, all through these chapters, for God's gift, for the believers' giving, and for Christ's own: the collection for Jerusalem is the same grace passed on. In v16 the same word is thanks.

  • v9 "though He was rich, for your sake He became poor, so that by His poverty you might become rich" — the whole story of Christ told in terms of money, the matter in hand. Paul tells it again in Philippians 2:6–7, though He was in the form of God… He emptied Himself, taking the form of a slave.

  • vv13–15 "fairness… The one who gathered much had nothing over, and the one who gathered little had no lack" — the manna, Exodus 16:18. God gave it so that each household had enough and no one hoarded; Paul makes it the rule for the churches' giving.

  • v21 "what is honorable not only in the Lord's sight but also in the sight of men" — Proverbs 3:4 in the Greek, pronoou kala enōpion Kyriou kai anthrōpōn, which Paul also used in Romans 12:17; the Hebrew has you will find favor and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
